title: Does charging overnight ruin your battery
caption:
Does charging overnight ruin your battery? Your phone may not even charge all night.
With its charging setting on, it can wait at 80% and finish right before you unplug. Your job: keep it cool, not under a pillow.
Is your phone set to wait? Yes or no.
keywords: does charging overnight ruin your battery
is it bad to charge your phone overnight
does charging overnight damage battery iphone
does charging overnight damage battery samsung
should i charge my phone overnight
charging phone overnight bad for battery
pinned_comment: Honest version: it only waits if the setting is on and has learned your routine (about 14 days), and heat still counts, so keep it out from under the pillow. Is your phone set to wait? Yes or no.

pinned_backups.if: So overnight charging is totally fine?
pinned_backups.reply: Not always. With the setting off, the phone can sit at 100% for hours, and Samsung US says to unplug "after the device has reached a 100% charge to avoid a swollen battery." With the setting on and the phone kept cool, the phone handles the long hours at full.

pinned_backups.if: Mine went straight to 100% last night.
pinned_backups.reply: That can happen. Apple says it delays past 80 percent "in certain situations" and needs at least 14 days and 9 long charges in one place to learn; Pixel says Adaptive Charging "may turn on". Check that the setting is on, and give it a couple of weeks of the same routine.

pinned_backups.if: Should I just set it to stop at 80%?
pinned_backups.reply: That's your call. iPhone 15 and later can set a charge limit from 80 to 100 percent, Pixel 6a and later have Limit to 80%, and Galaxy has Battery protection options. The trade is less battery for the day in return for less time at full.
Different topic, and we didn't cover it here. The same rule from Apple applies though: if the phone gets hot while it charges, take it out of its case and keep it somewhere with air around it.

youtube_description:
Does charging overnight ruin your battery? Your phone may not even charge all night. Two things speed up wear: heat, and long hours at full charge. With its charging setting on, your phone can hold back the last stretch and finish right before you usually unplug. It handles the hours; you handle the heat: charge it in the open, not under a pillow, out of a hot case.

Hours at 100%. Apple, "About Charge Limit and Optimized Battery Charging on iPhone": "A battery's chemical age results from a complex combination of several factors, including temperature history and charging pattern." Optimized Battery Charging "is designed to reduce the wear on your battery and improve its lifespan by reducing the time your iPhone spends fully charged." When it's on, "your iPhone will delay charging past 80 percent in certain situations." And: "The algorithm aims to ensure that your iPhone is still fully charged when unplugged."

Heat. Apple, "Maximizing Battery Life and Lifespan": "It's especially important to avoid exposing your device to ambient temperatures higher than 95° F (35° C), which can permanently damage battery capacity." On cases: "If you notice that your device gets hot when you charge it, take it out of its case first."

The pillow. Apple iPhone User Guide, "Important safety information for iPhone": "don't sleep on a device, power adapter, or wireless charger, or place them under a blanket, pillow, or your body, when it's connected to a power source."

Pixel. Google Pixel Help, "Get the most life from your Pixel phone battery": "Your phone warms up when it's plugged in, so don't keep it charging more than needed." On Adaptive Charging: "This setting completes charging right before you typically unplug, so your phone isn't at 100% for a long time. This can strain the battery long term." And: "When you charge your phone for a long time or overnight, Adaptive Charging may turn on to charge to 100% one hour before you unplug."

Galaxy. Samsung US, "Get the most out of your Galaxy phone or tablet battery," on Adaptive: "Once your device learns your routine, adaptive will automatically stop charging at 80%, and it will switch to Basic before you wake up." Samsung US, "Galaxy Battery: Care and Maintenance": "Unplug the charger after the device has reached a 100% charge to avoid a swollen battery." That's why we don't call overnight charging harmless.

How to check yours. iPhone 15 and later: Settings › Battery › Charging. iPhone 14 and earlier: Settings › Battery › Battery Health & Charging. Pixel: Settings › Battery › Battery health › Charging optimization. Galaxy: Settings › Battery › Battery protection › Adaptive. When it's on, iPhone and Pixel show when the phone will be fully charged. Menus vary by model.

Fine print: These features work "in certain situations" (Apple) and need time to learn: Apple says "at least 14 days" and at least 9 charges of 5 hours or more in one place; Google says about 14 days. Apple says Optimized Battery Charging "is on by default"; Pixel and Galaxy defaults vary, so check yours. The night in the video is an illustrative example; no source says when a phone reaches 80%. Apple's pillow line is safety advice; heat trapped under a pillow is our reading of it. The screens are re-created by hand; no real interface or logo is shown.
